reference.text: We suggest using EEN in critically ill adult patients rather than early PN (Grade 2C) or delaying EN (Grade 2C)
We suggest delaying EN if shock is uncontrolled and haemodynamic and tissue perfusion goals are not reached, but start low dose EN as soon as shock is controlled
We suggest delaying EN in case of uncontrolled life-threatening hypoxaemia, hypercapnia or acidosis, but using EEN in patients with stable hypoxaemia...
We suggest that EN should not be delayed solely because of the concomitant use of neuromuscular blocking agents
We suggest starting low dose EEN in patients receiving therapeutic hypothermia and increase the dose after rewarming
We suggest using EEN in adult patients receiving extracorporeal membrane oxygenation
We suggest that EN should not be delayed solely because of prone positioning
We suggest using EEN in critically ill adult patients with traumatic brain injury
We suggest using EEN in critically ill adult patients with stroke (ischaemic or haemorrhagic)
We suggest using EEN in critically ill adult patients with spinal cord injury
We suggest using EEN in critically ill adult patients with severe acute pancreatitis
We suggest using EEN in critically ill adult patients after gastrointestinal surgery
We suggest using EEN in critically ill adult patients after abdominal aortic surgery
We suggest using EEN in critically ill adult patients with abdominal trauma after the continuity of the GI tract is confirmed/restored
We suggest delaying EN in critically ill adult patients with overt bowel ischaemia
We suggest delaying EN in critically ill adult patients with high-output intestinal fistula if reliable feeding access distal to the fistula is not achievable
We suggest using EEN in critically ill adult patients with an open abdomen
We suggest using EEN in patients with intra-abdominal hypertension without abdominal compartment syndrome, but consider temporary reduction or discontinuation of EN...
We suggest delaying EN in critically ill adult patients with abdominal compartment syndrome
We suggest delaying EN in patients with active upper GI bleeding, and starting EN when the bleeding has stopped and no signs of rebleeding are observed
We suggest starting low dose enteral nutrition when acute, immediately life-threatening metabolic derangements are controlled with or without liver support strategies...
We suggest delaying EN in critically ill adult patients if gastric aspirate volume is above 500 ml/6 h
We suggest using EEN in critically ill adult patients regardless of the presence of bowel sounds unless bowel ischaemia or obstruction is suspected
We suggest using EEN in critically ill adult patients presenting with diarrhoea
Remark: We suggest considering early use of prokinetics followed by post-pyloric feeding in case of persisting gastric retention.
Remark: Arterial ammonia levels should be monitored.

notes: Reference = Table 2 (pp.3-4): 23 numbered recs with 18 split into 18a/18b = 24 items. Every item carries a GRADE strength ('conditional recommendation ... Grade 2C' or 'Grade 2D'); 'expert opinion' recs are Grade 2D = conditional, very low (methods p.2: expert opinion = very low quality evidence), so all are graded weak/for (direction 'for' = for the stated action, incl. 'delay EN'). Rec 1 is one sentence with two comparisons (vs early PN, vs delayed EN), each 2C: counted once. Ungraded items counted: the two formal body 'Remark' statements (Rec 7: prokinetics/post-pyloric feeding; Rec 20: monitor arterial ammonia); neither extracted. Excluded from reference: Table 1 general principles/precautions and prose 'we suggest/recommend' sentences inside rationale (e.g. diarrhoea causes, ACS withholding EN) - not stated as recommendations. All 16 FPs are body-text restatements (pp.7-16) not deduped against the Table 2 copies; several restated rows carry wrong certainty 'low' for 2D recs (rows 0,7,9,10,13,32,34,39) - irrelevant to TP scoring since table rows were matched. 'Weak For' raw_strength on rows 36-38 is extractor wording; harmonized same.
